valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 15 Nov 2026. (1) Business: a Sri Lankan commercial bank (banking is about 97% of group profit; NDB Investment Bank, NDB Securities, NDB Wealth and property the rest), so one sector beta. (2)–(3) A bank, so no relevering: the sector's levered beta, Damodaran's Bank (Money Center) 0.70 (January 2026, as used for SAMP; from a web-search extract, his site couldn't be opened). (4) Local betas: no source with a stated 5-year window could be opened. Used instead: the median of the five yearly betas against the ASPI that NDB itself publishes (Annual Report 2025, p. 520: 0.53, 0.63, 2.44, 1.24, 1.46 for 2021–2025) = 1.24; TradingView 1.60 (window not stated); Simply Wall St 0.70 (January 2025). Median of the three: 1.24. Traded on most days (72,275 trades in 2025), so not thin. (5) Higher of 0.70 and 1.24 = 1.24. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: replace with three verified 5-year betas in January 2027. At Damodaran's 0.70 the cost of equity would be 15.4% and fair value roughly 50–60% higher.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (15 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 1.24 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 21.0%, ±1.5 points. At the top of the 12–22% house range because the beta is high; the bear case is above it.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 3% / 5% / 7%; supported 3.9% (share of profit kept × ROE, FY 2025 restated: 46.1% × 8.38%). Bull 3.1 pts above: 2025 ROE is cut by the one-off fraud loss; on profit without the fraud, keeping 65% at a 13% ROE supports about 8.5%.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on the restated FY 2025 figures; earnings growth for the five years after 2027.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE (price to book)
valuationInputs.reason: Group ROE without the fraud: 12.5% (2021), 12.5% (2024), 13.6% (2025), about 13.5% in 9M 2026; 4.6–8.1% in 2022–2023. Bear allows for higher control costs and recoveries never coming; bull for NDB reaching the 15% of stronger peers.

valuationInputs.name: ROE path (residual income)
valuationInputs.reason: Over 10 years from about 12–13% today, then the excess return (negative while ROE is below the cost of equity) grows at the long-run rate.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: Below the 12.24% bond yield and the cost of equity; needs 45–47% of profit kept (growth ÷ ROE).

valuationInputs.name: 2027 EPS × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: Group EPS without fraud losses was about Rs 29.6 over the last 12 months; Q3 2026 × 4 = Rs 25.6. Base +5% on the higher run-rate (25.6) used by the calculator; NIM is falling (3.57% from 4.06%). P/Es equal the justified 3.3x / 3.8x / 4.6x at a 21% cost of equity.

valuationInputs.name: Dividends
valuationInputs.value: 35% of EPS for five years (bear: nothing for 2027), then 1 − growth ÷ ROE (55% / 54% / 53%)
valuationInputs.reason: NDB paid 31–37% of group EPS in 2021–2024, part in scrip; the CBSL suspended the 2025 cash dividend after the fraud.

openQuestions: What the CBSL decides on the suspended Rs 6.46 cash dividend for 2025, and whether cash dividends resume for 2026.
Any recoveries of the Rs 13.64bn fraud (would be booked as income) and the outcome of the CBSL's review.
CET1 (9.48%, Tier 1 minimum 8.5%): does it recover, or is a rights issue needed?
Net interest margin (3.57%) and the fall in CASA (20.7%): bottoming out?
Three verified local 5-year betas and Damodaran's January 2027 emerging-markets bank beta (the 1.24 beta is provisional).

changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/add NDB). First analysis from the four downloaded CSE reports (Annual Report 2025 and the Q1, H1 and 9M 2026 interims). The annual report predates the Rs 13.64bn fraud found in April 2026, so 2024–2025 figures use the restated numbers in the 9M 2026 interim (2024 EPS and ROE restated not published: first-reported figures kept with a note). Cost of equity 21.0% from a provisional beta of 1.24 (median of NDB's own yearly ASPI betas 2021–2025, TradingView 1.60, Simply Wall St 0.70; no verified 5-year beta could be opened). Price Rs 103.00 (5 Nov 2026) from an EconomyNext report: the CSE site was blocked in this run. Business tests 1 of 4 (fails returns, capital and cash dividends): avoid for now (category 3).
